$comment: MCP servers the harness launches as child processes and speaks stdio to.
This is the seam that makes the harness language-agnostic: these are all
Python, the harness is Rust, and neither cares.
COPY OF RECORD. The harness copies this to mcps/servers.json on first run
if that file is absent, then never touches it again - servers.json is
gitignored because it holds absolute paths to clones that live wherever
you put them. Edit servers.json, not this file.
Only the two servers that live inside this repo are enabled by default.
The other three need repos you have to clone yourself; each is left here,
disabled, with what it needs. A server that fails to start is reported and
skipped, so a wrong path costs you that server, never the assistant.
Paths are relative to the repo root unless absolute.
Graph memory. Ships in this repo; owns its own kuzu database and needs
no external daemon. Needs the .venv described in the README (kuzu +
mcp v2). On Linux/macOS the command is .venv/bin/python.
Code intelligence through Neovim's language servers. Ships in this repo.
No Python dependencies: it shells out to `nvim --headless -l` and parses
JSON. Needs Neovim 0.11+ on PATH (0.11 has a built-in LSP client, so no
lazy.nvim and no mason), plus a language server per language - it
registers only the ones actually present. `lsp_status` lists what it
found and how to add the rest.
codemap.rs answers 'where does X live'; this answers 'what calls X',
which needs real resolution rather than text matching.
Without Neovim installed this server simply fails to start and is
skipped. Nothing else breaks.
Pixel-level GUI control - 70 tools. DISABLED: needs a clone.
git clone https://github.com/chrisjaron03/UACC mcps/UACC
Then give it its OWN venv (mcps/UACC/.venv), not the harness venv:
UACC is written against mcp v1 (FastMCP) while the kuzu server needs
mcp v2 (MCPServer), and those cannot coexist in one interpreter.
Separate processes can have separate Pythons - which is exactly what
the MCP boundary buys us, and it matches what UACC's own uacc-mcp.bat
already expects (it looks for %~dp0.venv).
It also needs one upstream syntax patch to import at all - see
mcps/patches/README.md. Set enabled to true once both are done.
Local capture, embed and search - 31 tools. DISABLED: it is a separate
project and the path above must point at your own clone of it.
It is a stateless stdio proxy in front of a daemon on 127.0.0.1:8756.
Stdlib-only, so it needs no venv packages and starts regardless.
IMPORTANT: the daemon idles out and is restarted from the SnareVec
workbench. When it is down this server still connects and still lists
tools, but tool CALLS fail. That is a runtime condition, not a config
error - see persona/TOOLS.md for how the assistant should handle it.
A tool layer over Neovim via pynvim, exposed over MCP. DISABLED: the
entrypoint ships here but the tools it wraps live in a separate
nyx-nvim clone that is not vendored, and three of its modules need
version-tolerant patches on Neovim 0.11+ - see
mcps/patches/nyx-nvim-windows.md for exactly what and why.
It shares the Neovim that nvim_lsp keeps warm, and starts one itself
if needed.
NOTE: its refactor tools WRITE to files. Untick it per workspace in
+ menu -> Connectors for folders that should stay read-only.
